sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the duplication of the verse about the names of Israel coming to Egypt and its eternal lesson.

translations.translation: "And these are the names of the children of Israel coming to Egypt: Reuven, Shimon, Levi, and Yehudah..."1
And it is known the precise point of the Baal HaHilula
[of 24 Tevet — the Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe]
in his sefer Torah Or, in the discourse beginning with this phrase2,
that in Parshat Vayigash3
it is also stated: "And these are the names of the children of Israel coming to Egypt,"
and it must be understood why the matter of their coming to Egypt is repeated in the Torah.
And the Rebbe, the Mitteler Rebbe, adds further
[in this discourse in Torat Chayim4,
which is an explanation of the above-mentioned discourse of the Alter Rebbe and its elucidation5]
that it is known6
that the Torah is eternal and speaks in every time and in every generation,
meaning that also the matter of the coming to Egypt, etc., exists in every generation,
and likewise there is a lesson from this for every single Jew in every time and in every place,
for Torah is from the word "hora'ah" (teaching)7,
and thus the lesson is eternal.
And so,
since the Torah is eternal, it is understood that also the details of the matters of the Egyptian exile, etc., exist in every generation,
and therefore also the details of the matters of "and they embittered their lives with hard labor, with mortar and bricks... all their work which they worked through them with rigor"8,
also exist in all times.
And the intention in the matter of "and they embittered their lives," etc., is not for its own sake, Heaven forbid,
rather, that this matter exists only for the sake of the redemption, etc., that follows afterward.
And as it is stated9
"I will descend with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you up,"
meaning that the entire intention of the descent into Egypt, etc., is only so that afterward there will be "and I will surely bring you up."
